reading.stem: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks:
Dear Route Supervisor,
I take the number 16 from Pine Road to the station every weekday. At 7:40 yesterday I stood beside the stop sign with my hand raised. The bus passed with several empty seats. Two other passengers told me that the same thing had happened on Monday. The timetable still includes this stop, and there is no notice about roadwork. Please remind the morning drivers to pick up waiting passengers at Pine Road. I have enclosed the dates in case they help you identify the journeys concerned.
Yours faithfully, Irene Park
choices: 공사로 인한 우회 노선을 승객에게 공지하려고
운행 시각을 저녁으로 바꿔 달라고 요구하려고
아침 버스가 지정 정류장에 제대로 정차하도록 요청하려고
evidence: Please remind the morning drivers to pick up waiting passengers at Pine Road.
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 글의 목적
정류장과 시간표는 그대로인데 빈자리가 있는 버스가 승객을 지나쳤다. 글쓴이는 기사들이 이 정류장에서 승객을 태우도록 조치해 달라고 한다.
근거 “Please remind the morning drivers to pick up waiting passengers at Pine Road.”

reading.stem: 다음 글에 드러난 주인공의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: “Can I have another coin?” Ben asked just as I sat down to finish a report. I pushed back my chair harder than necessary. Hadn't he already spent his allowance at the neighborhood sale? He opened his palm. Beside a bent key ring lay one silver button, exactly like the button missing from my grandmother's coat. He had found a second one at the same table and wanted to buy it before someone else did. I pressed a coin into his hand, smiling at the thought he had put into his little errand. The report could wait.
evidence: I pressed a coin into his hand, smiling at the thought he had put into his little errand.
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 심경 변화
아이가 일을 방해한다고 느껴 짜증을 냈지만 가족의 옷에 맞는 단추를 찾았다는 사실에 마음이 움직였다.
근거 “I pressed a coin into his hand, smiling at the thought he had put into his little errand.”

reading.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A supervisor finds that a worker has submitted four reports after the deadline. Calling the worker careless may feel like an explanation, but it gives neither person a useful starting point. The worker might have misunderstood the schedule, or a machine might be unavailable at the end of the shift. A discussion can settle those questions. It is far harder to settle whether someone is, by nature, a careless person. Describe what happened, ask how it happened, and agree on what the employee can do differently next time. A change that both people can observe will be easier to assess.
choices: 기한을 넘긴 보고서는 원인을 묻지 말고 되돌려 보내야 한다.
직원의 문제를 지도할 때는 성격을 단정하기보다 구체적인 행동에 초점을 두어야 한다.
상호 평가에서는 업무 결과보다 관리자의 직감을 우선해야 한다.
직원 사이의 갈등은 당사자끼리만 해결하도록 해야 한다.
개인의 성격을 잘 알면 보고 절차를 점검할 필요가 없다.
evidence: Describe what happened, ask how it happened, and agree on what the employee can do differently next time.
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 필자의 주장
지각한 보고서는 확인 가능한 사건이지만 부주의하다는 성격 평가는 확인하기 어렵다. 행동을 구체적으로 파악하고 다음 행동을 합의하라는 주장이다.
근거 “Describe what happened, ask how it happened, and agree on what the employee can do differently next time.”

reading.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>keep a spare key under the soil</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
blocks: In a mixed forest, the fastest-growing trees may eventually shade their neighbors. A fungus attached to several kinds of roots faces a different problem. If it depended entirely on today's winner, a disease affecting that tree could cut off its only supply of food. Helping a slower-growing partner survive may therefore benefit the fungus later. In this sense the fungus seems to <u>keep a spare key under the soil</u>. There is no suggestion that it makes a conscious plan. Maintaining several living partners makes the fungus less dependent on the fate of any single species.
choices: prevent weaker trees from exchanging resources
favor the fastest-growing tree in every exchange
preserve alternative partners that may sustain it later
anticipate the precise date a disease will arrive
hide its food supply from every neighboring tree
evidence: Maintaining several living partners makes the fungus less dependent on the fate of any single species.
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 함축 의미
여분의 열쇠는 하나가 없어져도 쓸 수 있는 대안이다. 균류가 여러 수종과 연결되는 것은 한 수종에 문제가 생겼을 때 생존 가능성을 높인다.
근거 “Maintaining several living partners makes the fungus less dependent on the fate of any single species.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Picture yourself receiving a prize you hope to win. For a few pleasant seconds the work feels complete, although the blank application is still on your desk. That feeling explains a curious risk of imagining only the successful ending. The mind can enjoy part of the reward without paying any of the cost. Afterwards, beginning the actual task may feel less urgent. This need not happen whenever someone has a goal. It is the unbroken daydream, with every difficulty removed, that causes the trouble. A fantasy that supplies satisfaction in advance can drain the energy required to act.
choices: 성공의 즐거움을 미리 누리는 상상은 실제 행동의 동력을 약하게 할 수 있다.
결과를 반복해서 떠올릴수록 실제 노력도 반드시 늘어난다.
어려움을 예상하면 상상 속에서는 더 큰 보상을 느낀다.
목표를 구체적으로 정하면 성취의 기쁨도 줄어든다.
계획을 글로 쓰는 일은 목표에 대한 흥미를 낮춘다.
evidence: A fantasy that supplies satisfaction in advance can drain the energy required to act.
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 글의 요지
노력 없이 성공 장면만 즐기면 이미 보상을 받은 듯해 실제 일을 시작할 절박함이 줄 수 있다는 설명이다.
근거 “A fantasy that supplies satisfaction in advance can drain the energy required to act.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A cook in one household might need several hours to prepare a dish from another continent, especially if the ingredients are sold only in large quantities. A kitchen cooking for a hundred families can spread that time and cost across many portions. A customer who would never buy a whole jar of an unfamiliar spice can still try the dish for dinner. Much is lost when no one at home learns to cook. Yet that real loss can hide a different change. Moving some cooking outside the household has made unfamiliar foods accessible to people with limited time, money, or skill.
choices: the link between expensive kitchens and successful restaurants
the disappearance of regional flavors from restaurant menus
greater access to varied meals through shared commercial preparation
the need to buy unfamiliar ingredients in larger packages
the effects of formal culinary training on family relationships
evidence: Moving some cooking outside the household has made unfamiliar foods accessible to people with limited time, money, or skill.
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 글의 주제
가정 밖에서 한꺼번에 조리하면 비용과 시간을 나눌 수 있다. 이로 인해 소비자가 접할 수 있는 음식의 범위가 넓어진다는 점이 중심이다.
근거 “Moving some cooking outside the household has made unfamiliar foods accessible to people with limited time, money, or skill.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Two soap bars cost nearly the same. One maker refills old containers; the other surrounds each bar with layers of plastic. Buying either one may seem too small a decision to register beyond the bathroom. But a sale is also a message about which business practice can continue to earn money. When enough buyers investigate a manufacturer's record and act on what they find, that message becomes difficult for a company to ignore. The receipt records a choice about the market people wish to support as well as a purchase for their own home.
choices: The Secret History of Refillable Containers
What Your Shopping Basket Can Say to a Business
Why Manufacturers Always Set the Same Price
A Receipt That Guarantees Product Quality
evidence: The receipt records a choice about the market people wish to support as well as a purchase for their own home.
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 글의 제목
구매는 개인의 필요를 충족하면서 어떤 기업의 관행에 돈을 보낼지를 결정한다. 소비자가 구매로 기업에 보내는 신호를 포괄하는 제목이 알맞다.
근거 “The receipt records a choice about the market people wish to support as well as a purchase for their own home.”

reading.stem: 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

title: Internet Access Through Smart Televisions
blocks.note: Case study data for this exercise.

blocks: Households in each district reported whether anyone had used a television to go online during the previous month.
choices: One of the two figures for West was below 27.5%, and the other was above it.
For Coast, the figure for Autumn was above the figure for Spring.
For Spring, the figure for East exceeded that for Valley by 36 percentage points.
The two bars for Hill are 24 percentage points apart.
For Autumn, Valley ranked third highest among the five categories.
evidence: Valley: 22, 48
East: 55, 38
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 도표 내용 불일치
Spring에서 East(55%)와 Valley(22%)의 차이는 33%포인트이다.
[지문 근거] “Valley: 22, 48” / “East: 55, 38”

reading.stem: Camille Flammarion에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
blocks: At sixteen, Camille Flammarion had already filled a manuscript with his thoughts about the world's origins. Although it stayed out of print, the director of the Paris Observatory learned of it. There the young Frenchman later earned his living doing calculations. A book for general readers, Popular Astronomy, reached a much wider audience. Flammarion also paid for an observatory at Juvisy from his own pocket. He went on to establish an astronomical society in France and edit its monthly publication.
choices: 열여섯 살에 세계의 기원에 관한 원고를 썼다.
Juvisy의 천문대를 협회의 재정 지원으로 지었다.
evidence: paid for an observatory at Juvisy from his own pocket
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 내용 불일치
Juvisy 천문대 건립 비용은 자신이 부담했다.
[지문 근거] “paid for an observatory at Juvisy from his own pocket”

reading.stem: Distance Relay Week에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

blocks.title: Distance Relay Week
lines: Build a relay without traveling. A team can be spread across the country, as long as its members record the same activity on successive days.
Only the captain uploads the team's record when all members have finished.
A route may be indoors or outside.
Complete the four stages on four different days.
Every team that finishes receives a digital badge.

choices: 팀원 모두가 각자의 기록을 직접 올려야 한다.
완주한 모든 팀이 디지털 배지를 받는다.
네 구간을 각각 다른 날에 마쳐야 한다.
evidence: Only the captain uploads the team's record
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 안내문 내용 불일치
기록은 주장 한 명이 제출하므로 전원이 개별적으로 올린다는 설명은 맞지 않는다.
[지문 근거] “Only the captain uploads the team's record”

reading.stem: Ready for Monday에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

blocks.title: Ready for Monday
lines: The neighborhood center has collected school supplies. Families can choose the items their children still need before classes begin.
Bring the child who will use the supplies to the collection desk.
The hall opens at ten in the morning.
Families do not need to pay or book a ticket.
Each child may choose any two items.
Used uniforms are distributed in another building.

choices: 중고 교복도 같은 건물에서 나누어 준다.
모든 어린이가 세 가지씩 골라야 한다.
학용품을 사용할 아이가 수령 장소에 와야 한다.
evidence: Bring the child who will use the supplies
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 안내문 내용 일치
학용품을 실제 사용할 아이를 데리고 와야 한다.
[지문 근거] “Bring the child who will use the supplies”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3점]
blocks: On a shop shelf, the date ① <u>printed</u> on a package is easy to see. Far less visible ② <u>are</u> the miles the food has traveled. A shopper who throws a packet away simply because a recommended selling date has passed may also be discarding resources ③ <u>that</u> went into cooling and transporting it. Some stores now arrange shelves ④ <u>so</u> customers can reach older goods first. Others offer clearly marked discounts, giving customers a reason ⑤ <u>choose</u> items that would otherwise be removed at closing time.
evidence: giving customers a reason
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 어법
reason을 뒤에서 꾸며 선택할 이유라는 뜻을 내는 to부정사가 필요하다. 따라서 choose를 to choose로 고친다. 도치된 둘째 문장의 주어는 복수형 the miles이다.
[지문 근거] “giving customers a reason”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3점]
blocks: Two friends can drink coffee at the same time without having identical evenings. The body gradually ① <u>builds up</u> caffeine, and the speed of this process is not ② <u>uniform</u> from one person to the next. If one friend clears it slowly, a larger share of the original amount may ③ <u>remain</u> later in the day. For that person, counting only the cups overlooks a ④ <u>relevant</u> difference: the time the body takes to process each cup. Thus when clearance rates differ, the amounts remaining several hours after equal doses should generally be ⑤ <u>different</u>.
evidence: clears it slowly
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임
이 글은 섭취한 카페인이 시간이 흐르며 몸에서 제거되는 속도를 다룬다. builds up(축적한다)이 아니라 breaks down(분해한다)이 적절하다.
[지문 근거] “clears it slowly”

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks: A company sold two backpacks. Its advertisement for one called it the choice of practically every student. A small label on the other promised a bag for students who refused to follow the crowd. Both advertisements sent customers to the same checkout. The second campaign depended on the fact that <blank/> can be as predictable as obedience. Once the company knew which message would annoy a particular shopper, it could put the alternative exactly where that shopper would look. A student might choose freely between the two bags and still take the route the seller had prepared.
evidence: take the route the seller had prepared
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 빈칸 추론
남들이 택하는 가방에 대한 반발까지 예측해 두 번째 상품으로 유도했으므로 저항도 마케팅에 이용될 수 있다. 근거 표현은 “take the route the seller had prepared”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks: A television drama may introduce a dozen characters in ten minutes without explaining why a broken promise upsets anyone. Imagine trying the same trick with a board game whose rules the players have never seen. Even one move would require explanation. The contrast tells us why a complicated drama can feel easy. The viewer has already had years of practice with the rules behind it. A character who hides a letter from her sister makes sense because viewers know what it costs to lose someone's trust. Much of the work required to understand the invented family <blank/>.
choices: is performed by naming every character
disappears if the setting looks realistic
depends on hearing the actors' own histories
begins after the final episode is broadcast
was done outside the television program
evidence: viewers know what it costs to lose someone's trust
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 빈칸 추론
드라마의 관계를 이해하는 규칙은 신뢰와 약속을 다루며 살아온 시청자의 경험에서 이미 학습되었다. 근거 표현은 “viewers know what it costs to lose someone's trust”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점]
blocks: A hunting bat benefits when its call reveals a moth before the moth notices the bat. A moth benefits from detecting that very call in time to change direction. Now suppose that a moth population becomes sensitive to a wider range of calls. Bats using calls outside that range are more likely to catch dinner. As those calls become common, moths able to hear them have an advantage in turn. No member of either species needs to plan the next move. The sequence continues because a successful change on one side alters the challenge on the other. The two abilities must therefore be understood as <blank/>.
choices: evidence that a quieter habitat benefits both equally
stages that all flying animals pass through in order
responses that help shape each other's development
attempts by animals to teach signals to their young
solutions to two unrelated shortages of food
evidence: a successful change on one side alters the challenge on the other
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 빈칸 추론
나방의 탐지 능력은 박쥐의 사냥 조건을, 박쥐의 발성 변화는 다시 나방의 생존 조건을 바꾼다. 근거 표현은 “a successful change on one side alters the challenge on the other”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점]
blocks: Recall the last crowded station you walked through. You probably heard many voices, attended to a few words, and can now repeat even fewer. Your difficulty does not mean that your ears failed; a traveler who paused to process every announcement and conversation would miss the train. Attention gave some impressions priority. Memory retained only part of what attention selected, and an attempt at recall did not recover every retained detail. Seen together, these steps make thinking possible through <blank/>. At each step less material passes forward than was available at the beginning.
choices: successive reductions in the information being handled
a gradual increase in the number of surviving details
equal treatment of every signal reaching the traveler
repeated recording of the original sounds in full
the elimination of every impression unrelated to travel
evidence: less material passes forward than was available at the beginning
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 빈칸 추론
주의를 기울인 정보 중 일부만 저장되고 저장된 것 중 일부만 인출된다. 정보량을 단계마다 줄이는 것이 핵심이다. 근거 표현은 “less material passes forward than was available at the beginning”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
blocks: One route to representative government began with a ruler's empty treasury. ① A medieval king who lacked reliable information about harvests could not simply calculate and collect the money he wanted. ② Instead he invited local landholders to negotiate the sum they would contribute. ③ In return for their payment, the landholders could demand a say in how the money was spent. ④ Accountants often copy a total onto a second sheet in order to catch a slip in addition. ⑤ In this way the ruler's difficulty in raising revenue gave his subjects bargaining power.
evidence: the ruler's difficulty in raising revenue gave his subjects bargaining power
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 흐름과 무관한 문장
세입 확보가 어려운 통치자와 납세자의 협상이 대표 참여로 이어지는 과정이다. 덧셈을 검산하는 회계 습관은 그 과정에 속하지 않는다. 근거 표현은 “the ruler's difficulty in raising revenue gave his subjects bargaining power”이다.

reading.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Three bakeries open on the same street. Each pays to print a menu, and a student of economics points out that this spending adds to the cost of selling a loaf.
His second walk complicates that conclusion. One menu lists the hours when gluten-free rolls are baked, and another offers a discount on bread left after five.
With these details, a customer can choose a shop before joining a queue. Counting only the cost of printing would miss the time and effort that informative advertisements save.
On his first walk down the street, he sees almost identical signs promising excellent bread. He concludes that customers would be better off if the shops stopped printing advertisements altogether.
evidence: His second walk complicates that conclusion
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 글의 순서 (2점)
(C) - (A) - (B)의 순서이다. 첫 방문의 결론을 먼저 밝히고, 두 번째 방문에서 실용적인 메뉴 정보를 발견한 뒤 소비자가 절약하는 시간으로 그 의미를 풀이한다.
[지문 근거] “His second walk complicates that conclusion”

reading.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
blocks: A designer was asked to line a concert room with wooden panels. A lovely repeated pattern would have been easy to draw, but the echoes had to reach different seats at suitable times.
She first translated that demand into limits on the depth of each panel. Then she asked a program to explore the thousands of shapes permitted by those limits.

The finished wall therefore raises an awkward question about authorship. The instructions and the final judgment were hers, while the unexpected pattern between those two decisions came from a calculation.
Among the resulting possibilities was a surface that none of her preliminary drawings resembled. She kept its broad arrangement but softened several corners that were too hard to build.
evidence: Among the resulting possibilities
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 글의 순서 (3점)
(A) - (C) - (B)의 순서이다. 설계 조건 입력, 계산 결과 중 하나를 골라 수정, 완성품의 창작 주체에 대한 질문 순이다.
[지문 근거] “Among the resulting possibilities”

reading.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
blocks: One activity that promptly disappeared was her leisurely planning.

Before an ordinary lesson, Jina could follow a story while quietly planning her afternoon. ( ① ) During a fire drill, however, a smell of smoke made her suspect that this alarm might be real. ( ② ) She immediately searched for the nearest exit and listened for the teacher's directions. ( ③ ) It could be resumed after the danger passed, whereas a delay in finding an exit might matter now. ( ④ ) This is a useful way to think about attention under pressure. Urgent tasks claim resources that might otherwise support reflection. ( ⑤ ) Such narrowing may help someone leave a building quickly even though it makes a long discussion difficult at the same moment.
evidence: It could be resumed after the danger passed

정답 ③ · 문장 삽입 (2점)
위험에 집중하자 사라진 오후 계획을 제시해야 다음의 It could be resumed가 무엇을 나중에 다시 할 수 있다는 뜻인지 분명해진다.
[지문 근거] “It could be resumed after the danger passed”

reading.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3점]
blocks: This one pointed from a successful performance back toward a worker's interest.

A manager noticed that the people who seemed most interested in their work also produced the best results. ( ① ) She proposed workshops to make everyone feel engaged, expecting better performance to follow. ( ② ) Her adviser agreed that this sequence was possible but drew a second arrow on her chart. ( ③ ) Consider a new clerk who has struggled with customer requests for a month and finally settles a difficult case alone. ( ④ ) After that success, the clerk volunteers to handle calls that previously seemed exhausting. ( ⑤ ) A survey taken only at the end would find enthusiasm and achievement together but would miss the order in which they appeared.
evidence: a second arrow
Consider a new clerk
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 문장 삽입 (3점)
두 번째 화살표의 방향을 설명한 뒤 성공 경험이 흥미를 키우는 신입 직원 사례를 드는 흐름이다.
[지문 근거] “a second arrow” / “Consider a new clerk”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: After a flood, two volunteers each spent a Saturday sorting blankets. One said that working at the shelter eased the painful feeling of watching the news from home. The other wanted families to have dry bedding throughout the winter. When television coverage ended, the first volunteer felt less distressed and found it easy to stop. For the second, the end of the broadcasts did nothing to provide the missing bedding. She kept returning while the families still needed supplies. Identical first acts of help can therefore develop into quite different patterns of support.
Help motivated by another person's (A) may last beyond the point when the helper's own (B) has faded.
evidence: the first volunteer felt less distressed
the families still needed supplies
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 요약문 완성 (2점)
첫 사람의 행동은 자신의 불편함이 줄면서 멈췄지만, 두 번째 사람은 이재민의 필요가 남아 있는 동안 계속 도왔다.
[지문 근거] “the first volunteer felt less distressed” / “the families still needed supplies”

41-42.head: [41~42] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
blocks: A village once relied on a retired ferryman to explain where the river was shallow. His advice was (a) <u>scarce</u> knowledge: nobody had made a map, and few people had crossed in every season. When an engineer finally printed a chart, younger boat owners could obtain depths without asking him. The printed sheets thus made his advice (b) <u>indispensable</u> for looking up the old depths: a boat owner could now find every one of those figures without him. As a source of routine measurements the chart had ended his monopoly. Yet the engineer came back after a storm moved the channel. She needed someone who could (c) <u>interpret</u> a pattern of broken reeds along the bank. The old man could do that. The chart had (d) <u>removed</u> one reason for seeking his advice while exposing a different one. A new means of recording information may change which abilities command (e) <u>respect</u>; it need not make an entire generation either wiser or less useful.

43-45.head: [43~45] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
blocks: Eli spent afternoons at his uncle's repair shop. Everyone expected him to take it over, but the only job (a) <u>he</u> enjoyed was painting numbers on repaired bicycles. He hid a sketchbook under the till. One wet Friday his uncle found the book while looking for change.

With the bakery payment in hand, Eli rented a room above the shop. His uncle gave (b) <u>him</u> the old till for keeping receipts. Now when visitors asked whether (c) <u>he</u> had joined the family business, Eli invited them upstairs to see where his own work began.

The painted wheels attracted a bakery owner. She asked Eli for a price for (d) <u>her</u> window, but he had never quoted for a painting. Eli wrote down the hours and materials from the bicycle shop job before making an offer.

The first drawing was of the shop window. Eli expected a lecture; instead, his uncle asked (e) <u>him</u> to put the drawing on the glass. Eli agreed if he could change one thing: the flat lettering on the page would become a row of wheels.
